title: CryoSynapse - network airlock & key management sync
summary: Redwood AE/SE (Benji/Maya) walked CryoSynapse through proposed Private/VPC architecture for sensitive genomics workloads. Main focuses: strict egress controls with an airlock proxy, customer KMS integration (HSM optional), SSO/RBAC model, and audit log flow to customer SIEM. Customer asked for proof points on key rotation and offline key wraps, plus SOC 2 evidence for logging and access reviews. Agreed next steps: share SAML/OIDC integration notes, KMS onboarding runbook, and a short benchmark plan for pinned model to test egress performance.
next_steps: Benji to send SAML/OIDC integration guide and RBAC mapping example by 2026-10-28

Customer to prepare list of IP ranges and outbound destinations for egress allowlist by 2026-11-02
Schedule pilot kickoff (2-week) once KMS access is validated — tentatively 2026-11-08

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-21 11:00 PDT / 2026-10-21T18:00Z
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Benji Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Carlos E. (Redwood), Dr. Lena Ortiz (CTO, CryoSynapse), Samir Patel (Head Infra), Asha Iqbal (Security), Kevin Huang (DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, might be partial): Redwood and CryoSynapse discussed private deployment patterns, it's about VPC isolation and a network airlock pattern to control egress. KMS integration and SOC 2 evidence also in scope.

00:00 Benji Park: okay hi everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick intros — i'll hand it to maya for the network sketch in a minute.
00:18 Maya Singh: hey all, so i'll start with the high level. CryoSynapse wants private deploy inside their AWS account, oracle.. sorry (transcription) aws account, strict zero egress by default, only specific allowed egress to internal siem and the model fetching bucket. we're proposing an airlock proxy that sits in a dedicated egress subnet.
00:46 Samir Patel: yeah that sounds right. our big concern is processes that try to reach out to the public internet. we need proof that only the airlock can talk out and that we have audit trail for every outbound connection.
01:05 Maya Singh: absolutely. implementation-wise we support two modes: enforced egress through our managed egress proxy (hosted) tunneled through customer VPC egress nat gateway, or a customer-managed egress gateway we deploy as an image into their subnet — both can be configured with strict allowlists.
01:30 Dr. Lena Ortiz: what's the difference in terms of key material? do you keep any plaintext keys if we use your managed proxy?
01:42 Carlos Echeverri: good question. for managed egress the proxy needs to authenticate to Redwood control plane, but we can do that with mutual TLS and short-lived certs. we do not store customer KMS keys in plaintext. if you use customer KMS for model encryption and token sealing, only encrypted blobs are stored and decrypted in memory in worker processes.
02:08 Asha Iqbal: so, i need specifics on key rotation — we have a requirement for quarterly rotation and HSM-backed wrapping for root keys. can you do an HSM-backed flow?
02:22 Maya Singh: yes. we integrate with customer KMS providers (AWS KMS, CloudKMS, Azure Key Vault) and can also support an HSM on-prem wrapped key flow. the pattern is: root key stays in your HSM, we receive wrapped data keys via envelope encryption. rotation is orchestrated via a key versioning table and config in the private control plane.
02:48 Kevin Huang: sorry just one interruption — how do you handle key revocation in a stuck worker? if we rotate a key mid-run, will in-flight requests fail or keep working?
03:05 Maya Singh: great question. we support a grace window for key rotation: existing in-flight KV caches will use the old data key until they finish, and new requests fetch the new wrapped key. we also provide a forced rekey API if you want to flush. there is a short degrade window, but ops can tune the grace period.
03:34 Benji Park: a couple of notes on compliance evidence: we can provide SOC 2 runbooks, sample access logs, and change-history exports. our audit logs include token-level traces (subject to retention size). for ISO we have the policies but need to map them to your evidence matrix.
03:55 Dr. Lena Ortiz: on logs, we need to route all audit logs to our SIEM and have immutable retention for 7 years. can we ship logs directly to S3 in our account?
04:10 Maya Singh: yes, for Private deployments logs can be written to a customer S3 bucket or pushed via syslog/HTTPS to your SIEM endpoint. we also support a write-once option if you want object write permissions restricted. note: very long retention increases cost; we can show retention tiering.
04:38 Samir Patel: ingress question: how do models get pulled? we prefer a pull from our artifact repo rather than outbound from your control plane.
04:50 Carlos Echeverri: we can support a model pull agent that runs inside your cluster and pulls model artifacts from an internal artifact repo (e.g., internal S3 or artifactory) over private link. alternately, we can mirror models into your S3 with signed URLs. both approaches avoid public egress.
05:15 Asha Iqbal: for SSO and RBAC, we use Okta and expect SCIM for groups. can you do SCIM provisioning and map Okta groups to RBAC roles?
05:29 Benji Park: yes we support SAML and OIDC for authentication, SCIM for provisioning. typical mapping: okta group -> redwood role (admin/run/read-only). we'll share a sample claims mapping.
05:47 Kevin Huang: what about least privilege for operators — can we have time-limited access or break-glass?
05:55 Maya Singh: we have short-lived session tokens and can integrate with your existing tooling for break-glass; also audit trails will record assume-role actions. for emergency access we recommend ephemeral RBAC roles with approval workflow.
06:17 Benji Park: i'll note the customer requirement: quarterly key rotation, HSM root keys, 7-year immutable logs, SCIM/Okta, and egress-only-through-airlock.
06:30 Dr. Lena Ortiz: what about network policy enforcement on pods? we use calico with egress deny policies — will your sidecar or agent comply?
06:43 Maya Singh: yes, our deployment can be a daemonset that respects existing network policies. if you run a fully isolated nodegroup for inference, we can restrict the node egress to only the egress subnet. small caveat: we require a KV cache port open internally for model state. we'll document ports.
07:08 Samir Patel: we also need an offline test — can we run an airgapped dry-run where the control plane has no outbound access and we validate that inference nodes only talk to internal endpoints?
07:24 Carlos Echeverri: we can do a dry-run. the plan: deploy private control plane with control-plane access via bastion, disable external egress in a staging VPC, run synthetic traffic and capture network flows. we'll provide a checklist.
07:43 Asha Iqbal: on the SOC 2 angle, do you have a SOC 2 report for 2026? and can you surface the necessary PCC/CC controls for our auditors?
07:56 Benji Park: yes we have a SOC 2 Type II report for 2026 Q2. we can share an encrypted copy under an NDA and an evidence map that links Redwood controls to common control requirements.
08:12 Dr. Lena Ortiz: wonderful. any performance impact from airlock proxy? our latency SLOs are 50ms p50 for short prompts.
08:25 Maya Singh: the proxy adds microseconds if it's local; the main overhead is extra TCP hop and TLS. for sub-100ms SLOs we recommend colocated proxy in same AZ and continuous batching tuning in the runtime. we'll include a benchmark plan for your pinned model.
08:47 Samir Patel: are there any known gotchas on egress allowlist with managed DNS resolution? we want to avoid leaks via DNS over 53 to outside.
09:00 Maya Singh: we advise forcing internal DNS resolvers and blocking outbound 53. our agent uses SRV and internal resolvers; we'll include a recommended iptables/SG list.
09:18 Benji Park: i'll recap: deliver SAML/SCIM guide, KMS runbook + HSM options, model pull agent doc, and a dry-run checklist. can we agree on timelines?
09:33 Dr. Lena Ortiz: yes, the timelines look fine; we'll target the pilot in early November.
09:40 Kevin Huang: quick note i need the explicit list of ports and service FQDNs for our firewall team.
09:48 Maya Singh: will include a port matrix and FQDN list.
09:53 Benji Park: great, thanks everyone. ending notes: i'll follow up with the docs and schedule the pilot kickoff.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: speaker overlaps and proper nouns may be slightly garbled; some Redwood internal term like "KV cache" was transcribed correctly, others like "control plane" occasionally became "control plain".
